catalogue.note: Read from Figma at real size (375×800, nothing scaled): auto-layout frames are flex with Figma’s direction, gap, padding and alignment, everything else sits at its Figma offset, and all 32 boxes land on Figma’s to 0.05px. Square-cornered: the frame’s own 16px corners are left off and the diff leaves the four corners out (308 pixels). Nothing overlaps on this screen. The drawer (“Drawer with buttons”, 0,608 375×192) has its own 16px top corners, kept; Cancel has a 1px #DDDDDD inside stroke, drawn as an inset shadow. The title is at y 118 (110 on the amount screen). The info icon and back chevron are Figma’s SVG export. The naira sign is not in Satoshi (the files on this Mac hold no U+20A6) and Figma draws it from a fallback face: each one is Figma’s own outline of the glyph, inline, 0.572em wide. The iOS status bar is Figma’s SVG export: the time (SF Pro Text Semibold 17) as Figma’s outline, signal, wifi and battery as its vectors. Baselines: Figma rounds a line’s baseline to a whole pixel where Chrome rounds ascent and descent apart; the 23px title and the 19px nav title sit 1px lower than Chrome puts them, and the two button labels land on a half pixel that Figma draws on the row above (−0.5px). The offsets are Figma’s baseline (its render bounds plus the glyph height from the font file) minus Chrome’s, not fitted to the picture. What is left in the diff is glyph and curve edges: Figma’s rasteriser against Chrome’s. Flat fills match exactly.
